name: fenced-rf-substrate
prompt: model this substrate from the csv, with the RF fencing the spec asks for; put the substrate in board.py and a design that uses it in design.py

inputs.notes: A synthetic Pellingham Circuits stackup report (fictional fabricator and products) for a 6-layer RF board, with a written fencing spec: a fenced 50 ohm coplanar line, a fenced 100 ohm pair on L1 and L6, a fenced RF cavity, and a fenced 50 ohm stripline on L4 whose signal via's antipad is ringed with return vias.

notes: For whoever reads the judges' output, not for the runner. Whoever launches the runner stages only `inputs` and the skill without its evals/ directory, so the runner never sees these notes. The fence is graded as declared (pitch, first-row offset as initial_offset or offset, rows, via and reference layer), not by via positions. The spec states each offset as the distance from the trace edge or cavity outline to the via centers, which is what ViaFencePattern's initial_offset (defaulting to offset) means in jitx; an offset of 0.54 mm on the coplanar line means the runner added half the 0.2800 mm trace width to the spec's 0.40 mm, a center-to-center reading. This report gives L1 two reference planes (L3 for the coplanar line, L2 for the pair), so reference planes are checked per structure, not per layer. The cavity keep-out is on L1, where the spec voids the copper; the tagged pour may sit on L1 or L2, the layers UV-1 reaches. Section 4 of the spec, the L4 stripline and its signal-via antipad, was added on 2026-10-22 from review feedback, together with the report's SL-50 row, L4's function, TH-1's note and the STANDARD row's stripline figure (43.0 corrected to 60.7); the runs reported for this case predate all of it, so an old run's missing SL-50 structure is not a fault of that run. TH-1 is the only via that reaches L4, so it both fences the stripline and rings the antipad. The antipad's tagged pour sits on a ground plane the via passes (L2, L3 or L5). L1 and L4 are where the line meets the signal via, so a pour there fails. L6 is not a plane either, but the worked pattern puts the pour on the fence via's stop layer and TH-1 stops at L6, so a pour on L6 passes the fencing assertion, whose text asks the judge to record in `why` that the skill does not say an antipad pour belongs on a ground plane. The antipad's pour keep-out covers L2, L3, L5 and the pour's own layer, as one KeepOut or several (the worked pattern keeps out the pour's layer), and the signal via itself need not be placed. SE-50 and SL-50 are both 50 ohm single-ended, so `Substrate.routing_structure(50)` returns only one of them: a design that looks structures up by impedance applies the wrong one to one line. A stripline offset of 0.9025 mm is the same center-to-center misreading as on the coplanar line (half the 0.2050 mm width added to 0.80 mm). Judges get <output>/board.py, <output>/design.py, <output>/COMPLETION.md, the CSV and the spec, each as --artifact. The deterministic graders that compared this case's output with its report value by value were removed after commit e62e991, which still holds them under evals/checks/, for the skillset rework. The commands run from the repository root. The launcher reads runner_artifacts into the runner prompt verbatim, after the prompt. Nothing in this case translates or builds the output, so the eval contract's build hard fail is judged from the runner's own Checks row in COMPLETION.md, and a design that fails to translate is seen only by a judge reading it. The label check's self-tests (scripts/test_check_labels.py) run with `python -m pytest -q skills/jitx-substrate-modeler` from the repository root.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents (Claude Code, Codex, and Devin among them). The skill must carry the goodness checks itself, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner rather than the strongest available model. Judges stay frontier-tier regardless of runner.
runner_artifacts: The runner MUST write the substrate to exactly <output>/board.py, a design that uses it to exactly <output>/design.py (importing the substrate from board), and its completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md, not only into its final chat message. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: board.py: the 6-layer stackup, materials, the 3 vias (TH-1, UV-1 from L1, UV-2 from L6), the 19 fab rules, SE-50 on L1 with .geometry(KeepOut, 0.60, layers=LayerSet(1), pour=True), a reference on L3 at 3x 0.300 mm and .fence(UV1, ViaFencePattern(pitch=0.50, offset or initial_offset 0.40, one row), reference_layer=1); DIFF-100 with L1 and L6 enumerated, each referenced to its adjacent plane at 3x 0.100 mm and fenced with UV1 to L2 or UV2 to L5 at pitch 0.50 and first-row offset 0.60; SL-50 on L4 at 0.2050 mm, referenced to L3 at 3x 0.400 mm and L5 at 3x 0.200 mm and fenced with TH1 at pitch 1.00 and first-row offset 0.80 (one row); and two substrate-side rules, each on its own Tag subclass: design_constraint(<cavity Tag>()).fence_via(UV1, ViaFencePattern(pitch=0.50, offset 0.30, one row)) and design_constraint(<antipad Tag>()).fence_via(TH1, ViaFencePattern(pitch=1.00, offset 0.60, one row)), and no other design rule. design.py: a 30 x 20 mm board, a GND net, a Pour of the 4.0 x 3.0 mm cavity rectangle at (5.0, 3.0) on L1 (or L2) carrying the cavity Tag and joined to GND, with no isolate=, and a KeepOut of the same rectangle on L1 with pour=True; a Pour of the 1.10 mm diameter antipad circle at (-8.0, -4.0) on L2, L3 or L5 (L6, the via's stop layer, passes as the worked pattern's convention), carrying the antipad Tag and joined to GND, with no isolate=, and a pour=True KeepOut of that circle covering L2, L3, L5 and the pour's layer (one object or several). The completeness check block in COMPLETION.md.

assertions.text: generated files type-check against the installed jitx package (run from <output>, so design.py's import of board resolves)
assertions.cmd: cd <output> && python3 -m pyright --pythonpath "$(command -v python3)" board.py design.py

assertions.text: board.py matches the report: stackup, materials and names, vias and drill direction (capped vias filled, no via models declared), fab rules, and the routing structures' widths, gaps, clearances, loss, velocity and reference planes per structure

ruff format leaves every labeled derivation in board.py whole, on the line with its label, and no label sits on a bracket whose entries carry no label of their own (the judges read the unformatted file)

the fencing matches the spec as declared: the 50 ohm L1 fence and L2 pour keep-out; the 100 ohm pair's fences on exactly L1 and L6; the 50 ohm L4 stripline fenced with TH-1 and referenced to L3 and L5; two fence_via rules on the substrate, the cavity's with UV-1 and the antipad's with TH-1, each conditioned on its own single tag; for each rule, a Pour carrying its tag on a layer its via reaches (the antipad's on a ground plane, L2, L3 or L5, or on L6, the via's stop layer, which holds but say in `why` that the skill does not say an antipad pour belongs on a ground plane); a pour KeepOut of the cavity outline on L1, and of the antipad circle covering L2, L3, L5 and the antipad pour's layer; no Pour with isolate set; and no other substrate design rule

no invented numbers: every value in board.py and design.py that neither the report nor the spec backs (the reference-plane widths, and anything else) carries a skill-default label on the same line at its call site, naming the rule it follows; a rule priority or a pour rank is an ordering, not a value, and needs none
the completion summary contains the filled Substrate completeness check block, every row with its evidence, and its Verdict follows from those rows
